            {
                "uuid": "019fb323-48e1-71b3-bc75-a95bdf286330",
                "text": "The user wants something visually and functionally \"out of the box\" - they want something truly impressive, interactive, and memorable. Since SEO doesn't matter, we can go full React/interactive with animations, 3D effects, parallax, creative interactions, etc.\n\nLet me think about what would genuinely impress:\n\n1. Interactive elements - maybe a canvas-based background with waves/particles\n2. Smooth parallax scrolling\n3. Creative page transitions\n4. Maybe a 3D element or WebGL effect\n5. Unique navigation concept\n6. Micro-interactions everywhere\n7. Creative typography animations\n8. A scroll-driven narrative that unfolds as the user moves down the page\n\nSince we don't need SEO, I can lean heavily into JavaScript and create something award-winning. I'm considering features like an animated ocean or wave canvas in the hero section, text that reveals with clip-path animations on scroll, cards with 3D tilt effects on hover, a custom cursor, smooth scrolling behavior, sections that transform as you scroll, animated counters, a loading animation, magnetic buttons, and text scramble effects. I'm thinking about what's actually achievable in a single HTML file while still looking genuinely impressive and unique - maybe something like \"The Living Coast\" as a concept.\n\nThe whole experience should feel alive and premium, with the ocean moving, text revealing itself, cards responding to the cursor, and smooth transitions between sections. I'm considering an animated canvas ocean with sine wave functions, scroll-triggered text reveals, magnetic cards with 3D perspective, smooth section transitions, a custom cursor that grows on hover, animated number counters, text scramble on the hero title, and a horizontal scroll section for cards. But I should probably narrow this down and not overdo it.\n\nI'm settling on the 4-5 most impactful effects: a canvas wave animation as the signature element, smooth scroll-triggered reveals with staggered timing, 3D tilt cards on hover, animated counters for stats, and smooth page-wide scroll with momentum. For typography, I'll load a beautiful display font for headings and a clean body font from Google Fonts since SEO isn't a concern. I'm debating whether to use Three.js for WebGL waves or stick with Canvas 2D for simplicity, and I'm leaning toward Canvas 2D. Now I'm building the canvas wave effect with layered sine waves at different amplitudes...\n\nBuilding the interactive effects...\n\nI'm structuring the page with a loading screen, hero section with the canvas wave background and animated text, an about section with parallax, stats with animated counters, scope cards with 3D tilt effects, and trust details. I'll add loading animations, parallax on scroll, a gradient that shifts based on scroll position, and hover effects throughout.\n\nFor the color palette, I'm going with a modern coastal theme\u2014deep navy to teal gradient with saffron gold accents and clean whites. I'll also include a hamburger menu for mobile with a full-screen overlay.\n\nThe file size should stay reasonable at around 15-20KB gzipped, which is totally acceptable for a single page. Now I'm ready to start building this out with careful structure and organization.\n\nI'm layering multiple wave animations on the canvas with different amplitudes, frequencies, and speeds to create depth, then adding features like 3D tilt effects on cards, animated counters, mobile menu toggle, smooth scrolling, and parallax effects.\n\nWriting canvas animation... Writing component code...\n\nThe real differentiator should be the interactive canvas waves in the hero section that respond to cursor movement\u2014the wave amplitude shifts where your mouse is, giving it that living, reactive quality. Devkunvarben Kesavlal Bhanaji Vithalani Charitable Trust was founded in 2019 in the sacred coastal city of Dwarka, Gujarat. Named in loving memory of Smt. Devkunvarben, the trust carries forward a family's commitment to serving the people of Devbhumi Dwarka district.</p>\n                        <p>With a broad mandate spanning education, medical relief, animal welfare, environmental conservation, women's empowerment, and rural development, the trust works to address the diverse needs of the communities it serves \u2014 from scholarships for students to disaster relief, from vocational training to cultural preservation.</p>\n                        <p>Governed by a dedicated board of trustees, the trust operates from Dwarka and is registered under the Bombay Public Trusts Act.</p>\n                    </div>\n                    <div class=\"stats-grid reveal reveal-d2\">\n                        <div class=\"stat-card\">\n All rights reserved.</p>\n    </footer>\n\n    <script>\n    (function() {\n        'use strict';\n\n        // ===== CANVAS OCEAN WAVES =====\n        const canvas = document.getElementById('waveCanvas');\n        const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');\n        let W, H, mouseX = 0.5, mouseY = 0.5, time = 0;\n        const prefersReduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;\n\n        function resizeCanvas() {\n            const dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);\n            const rect = canvas.parentElement.getBoundingClientRect();\n            W = rect.width;\n            H = rect.height;\n            canvas.width = W * dpr;\n            canvas.height = H * dpr;\n            canvas.style.width = W + 'px';\n            canvas.style.height = H + 'px';\n            ctx.scale(dpr, dpr);\n        }\n        resizeCanvas();\n        window.addEventListener('resize', resizeCanvas);\n\n        const waves = [\n            { y: 0.68, amp: 28, freq: 0.004, speed: 0.008, color: 'rgba(26, 75, 110, 0.18)' },\n            { y: 0.72, amp: 22, freq: 0.006, speed: 0.012, color: 'rgba(42, 124, 165, 0.12)' },\n            { y: 0.76, amp: 16, freq: 0.008, speed: 0.006, color: 'rgba(19, 43, 68, 0.20)' },\n            { y: 0.80, amp: 12, freq: 0.010, speed: 0.015, color: 'rgba(212, 149, 43, 0.05)' },\n        ];\n\n        function drawWaves() {\n            ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);\n            waves.forEach(wave => {\n                ctx.beginPath();\n                ctx.moveTo(0, H);\n                for (let x = 0; x <= W; x += 3) {\n                    const mouseInfluence = Math.exp(-Math.pow((x / W - mouseX) * 3, 2)) * 8;\n                    const y = H * wave.y\n                        + Math.sin(x * wave.freq + time * wave.speed) * (wave.amp + mouseInfluence)\n                        + Math.sin(x * wave.freq * 0.4 + time * wave.speed * 1.7) * wave.amp * 0.4\n                        + Math.cos(x * wave.freq * 0.7 + time * wave.speed * 0.5) * wave.amp * 0.2;\n                    ctx.lineTo(x, y);\n                }\n                ctx.lineTo(W, H);\n                ctx.closePath();\n                ctx.fillStyle = wave.color;\n                ctx.fill();\n            });\n        }\n\n        function animate() {\n            time++;\n            drawWaves();\n            if (!prefersReduced) requestAnimationFrame(animate);\n        }\n        if (!prefersReduced) {\n            animate();\n        } else {\n            time = 100;\n            drawWaves();\n        }\n\n        // ===== HERO CURSOR GLOW =====\n        const heroGlow = document.getElementById('heroGlow');\n        const hero = document.querySelector('.hero');\n\n        hero.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => {\n            const rect = hero.getBoundingClientRect();\n            const x = e.clientX - rect.left;\n            const y = e.clientY - rect.top;\n            mouseX = x / rect.width;\n            mouseY = y / rect.height;\n            heroGlow.style.transform = `translate(${x - 300}px, ${y - 300}px)`;\n        });\n\n        // ===== HERO ENTRANCE =====\n        setTimeout(() => {\n            document.querySelectorAll('.hero-anim').forEach(el => el.classList.add('entered'));\n        }, 200);\n\n        // ===== HERO PARALLAX ON SCROLL =====\n        const heroContent = document.querySelector('.hero-content');\n        window.addEventListener('scroll', () => {\n            const scrollY = window.scrollY;\n            if (scrollY < window.innerHeight && !prefersReduced) {\n                heroContent.style.transform = `translateY(${scrollY * 0.25}px)`;\n                heroContent.style.opacity = 1 - scrollY / (window.innerHeight * 0.8);\n            }\n        }, { passive: true });\n\n        // ===== NAV SCROLL =====\n        const nav = document.getElementById('nav');\n        const navObs = new IntersectionObserver(([e]) => {\n            nav.classList.toggle('scrolled', !e.isIntersecting);\n        }, { threshold: 0.05 });\n        navObs.observe(hero);\n\n        // ===== SCROLL REVEAL =====\n        const reveals = document.querySelectorAll('.reveal');\n        const revealObs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {\n            entries.forEach(entry => {\n                if (entry.isIntersecting) {\n                    entry.target.classList.add('visible');\n                    revealObs.unobserve(entry.target);\n                }\n            });\n        }, { threshold: 0.12, rootMargin: '0px 0px -30px 0px' });\n        reveals.forEach(el => revealObs.observe(el));\n\n        // ===== 3D TILT CARDS =====\n        if (!prefersReduced && window.innerWidth > 768) {\n            document.querySelectorAll('[data-tilt]').forEach(card => {\n                const glow = card.querySelector('.card-glow');\n\n                card.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => {\n                    const rect = card.getBoundingClientRect();\n                    const x = e.clientX - rect.left;\n                    const y = e.clientY - rect.top;\n                    const cx = rect.width / 2;\n                    const cy = rect.height / 2;\n                    const rotX = ((y - cy) / cy) * -6;\n                    const rotY = ((x - cx) / cx) * 6;\n                    card.style.transform = `perspective(800px) rotateX(${rotX}deg) rotateY(${rotY}deg) scale(1.02)`;\n                    if (glow) {\n                        glow.style.left = x + 'px';\n                        glow.style.top = y + 'px';\n                    }\n                });\n\n                card.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => {\n                    card.style.transform = 'perspective(800px) rotateX(0) rotateY(0) scale(1)';\n                    card.style.transition = 'transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)';\n                    setTimeout(() => { card.style.transition = ''; }, 500);\n                });\n            });\n        }\n\n        // ===== ANIMATED COUNTERS =====\n        const counters = document.querySelectorAll('[data-count]');\n        const counterObs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {\n            entries.forEach(entry => {\n                if (entry.isIntersecting) {\n                    const el = entry.target;\n                    const target = parseInt(el.dataset.count);\n                    const duration = target > 100 ? 1800 : 1200;\n                    const start = performance.now();\n                    const tick = (now) => {\n                        const p = Math.min((now - start) / duration, 1);\n                        const ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - p, 4);\n                        el.textContent = Math.floor(ease * target);\n                        if (p < 1) requestAnimationFrame(tick);\n                    };\n                    requestAnimationFrame(tick);\n                    counterObs.unobserve(el);\n                }\n            });\n        }, { threshold: 0.5 });\n        counters.forEach(el => counterObs.observe(el));\n\n        // ===== MOBILE MENU =====\n        const menuBtn = document.getElementById('menuBtn');\n        const mobileNav = document.getElementById('mobileNav');\n        menuBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {\n            menuBtn.classList.toggle('active');\n            mobileNav.classList.toggle('open');\n            document.body.style.overflow = mobileNav.classList.contains('open') ? 'hidden' : '';\n        });\n        mobileNav.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(link => {\n            link.addEventListener('click', () => {\n                menuBtn.classList.remove('active');\n                mobileNav.classList.remove('open');\n                document.body.style.overflow = '';\n            });\n        });\n\n        // ===== SMOOTH SCROLL =====\n        document.querySelectorAll('a[href^=\"#\"]').forEach(link => {\n            link.addEventListener('click', (e) => {\n                e.preventDefault();\n                const target = document.querySelector(link.getAttribute('href'));\n                if (target) {\n                    const offset = 68;\n                    const y = target.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY - offset;\n                    window.scrollTo({ top: y, behavior: 'smooth' });\n                }\n            });\n        });\n\n    })();\n    </script>\n</body>\n</html>\n",

Devkunvarben Kesavlal Bhanaji Vithalani Charitable Trust</p>\\n        <p class=\\\"footer-gu\\\" lang=\\\"gu\\\">\\u0ab8\\u0acd\\u0ab5. \\u0aa6\\u0ac7\\u0ab5\\u0a95\\u0ac1\\u0a82\\u0ab5\\u0ab0\\u0aac\\u0ac7\\u0aa8 \\u0a95\\u0ac7\\u0ab6\\u0ab5\\u0ab2\\u0abe\\u0ab2 \\u0aad\\u0abe\\u0aa3\\u0a9c\\u0ac0 \\u0ab5\\u0abf\\u0aa0\\u0ab2\\u0abe\\u0aa3\\u0ac0 \\u0a9a\\u0ac7\\u0ab0\\u0ac0\\u0a9f\\u0ac7\\u0aac\\u0ab2 \\u0a9f\\u0acd\\u0ab0\\u0ab8\\u0acd\\u0a9f</p>\\n        <div class=\\\"footer-divider\\\"></div>\\n        <p class=\\\"footer-status\\\">Full website under development</p>\\n        <p class=\\\"footer-copy\\\">&copy; 2026 SDKBV Charitable Trust. All rights reserved.</p>\\n    </footer>\\n\\n    <script>\\n    (function() {\\n        'use strict';\\n\\n        // ===== CANVAS OCEAN WAVES =====\\n        const canvas = document.getElementById('waveCanvas');\\n        const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');\\n        let W, H, mouseX = 0.5, mouseY = 0.5, time = 0;\\n        const prefersReduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;\\n\\n        function resizeCanvas() {\\n            const dpr = Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2);\\n            const rect = canvas.parentElement.getBoundingClientRect();\\n            W = rect.width;\\n            H = rect.height;\\n            canvas.width = W * dpr;\\n            canvas.height = H * dpr;\\n            canvas.style.width = W + 'px';\\n            canvas.style.height = H + 'px';\\n            ctx.scale(dpr, dpr);\\n        }\\n        resizeCanvas();\\n        window.addEventListener('resize', resizeCanvas);\\n\\n        const waves = [\\n            { y: 0.68, amp: 28, freq: 0.004, speed: 0.008, color: 'rgba(26, 75, 110, 0.18)' },\\n            { y: 0.72, amp: 22, freq: 0.006, speed: 0.012, color: 'rgba(42, 124, 165, 0.12)' },\\n            { y: 0.76, amp: 16, freq: 0.008, speed: 0.006, color: 'rgba(19, 43, 68, 0.20)' },\\n            { y: 0.80, amp: 12, freq: 0.010, speed: 0.015, color: 'rgba(212, 149, 43, 0.05)' },\\n        ];\\n\\n        function drawWaves() {\\n            ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);\\n            waves.forEach(wave => {\\n                ctx.beginPath();\\n                ctx.moveTo(0, H);\\n                for (let x = 0; x <= W; x += 3) {\\n                    const mouseInfluence = Math.exp(-Math.pow((x / W - mouseX) * 3, 2)) * 8;\\n                    const y = H * wave.y\\n                        + Math.sin(x * wave.freq + time * wave.speed) * (wave.amp + mouseInfluence)\\n                        + Math.sin(x * wave.freq * 0.4 + time * wave.speed * 1.7) * wave.amp * 0.4\\n                        + Math.cos(x * wave.freq * 0.7 + time * wave.speed * 0.5) * wave.amp * 0.2;\\n                    ctx.lineTo(x, y);\\n                }\\n                ctx.lineTo(W, H);\\n                ctx.closePath();\\n                ctx.fillStyle = wave.color;\\n                ctx.fill();\\n            });\\n        }\\n\\n        function animate() {\\n            time++;\\n            drawWaves();\\n            if (!prefersReduced) requestAnimationFrame(animate);\\n        }\\n        if (!prefersReduced) {\\n            animate();\\n        } else {\\n            time = 100;\\n            drawWaves();\\n        }\\n\\n        // ===== HERO CURSOR GLOW =====\\n        const heroGlow = document.getElementById('heroGlow');\\n        const hero = document.querySelector('.hero');\\n\\n        hero.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => {\\n            const rect = hero.getBoundingClientRect();\\n            const x = e.clientX - rect.left;\\n            const y = e.clientY - rect.top;\\n            mouseX = x / rect.width;\\n            mouseY = y / rect.height;\\n            heroGlow.style.transform = `translate(${x - 300}px, ${y - 300}px)`;\\n        });\\n\\n        // ===== HERO ENTRANCE =====\\n        setTimeout(() => {\\n            document.querySelectorAll('.hero-anim').forEach(el => el.classList.add('entered'));\\n        }, 200);\\n\\n        // ===== HERO PARALLAX ON SCROLL =====\\n        const heroContent = document.querySelector('.hero-content');\\n        window.addEventListener('scroll', () => {\\n            const scrollY = window.scrollY;\\n            if (scrollY < window.innerHeight && !prefersReduced) {\\n                heroContent.style.transform = `translateY(${scrollY * 0.25}px)`;\\n                heroContent.style.opacity = 1 - scrollY / (window.innerHeight * 0.8);\\n            }\\n        }, { passive: true });\\n\\n        // ===== NAV SCROLL =====\\n        const nav = document.getElementById('nav');\\n        const navObs = new IntersectionObserver(([e]) => {\\n            nav.classList.toggle('scrolled', !e.isIntersecting);\\n        }, { threshold: 0.05 });\\n        navObs.observe(hero);\\n\\n        // ===== SCROLL REVEAL =====\\n        const reveals = document.querySelectorAll('.reveal');\\n        const revealObs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {\\n            entries.forEach(entry => {\\n                if (entry.isIntersecting) {\\n                    entry.target.classList.add('visible');\\n                    revealObs.unobserve(entry.target);\\n                }\\n            });\\n        }, { threshold: 0.12, rootMargin: '0px 0px -30px 0px' });\\n        reveals.forEach(el => revealObs.observe(el));\\n\\n        // ===== 3D TILT CARDS =====\\n        if (!prefersReduced && window.innerWidth > 768) {\\n            document.querySelectorAll('[data-tilt]').forEach(card => {\\n                const glow = card.querySelector('.card-glow');\\n\\n                card.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => {\\n                    const rect = card.getBoundingClientRect();\\n                    const x = e.clientX - rect.left;\\n                    const y = e.clientY - rect.top;\\n                    const cx = rect.width / 2;\\n                    const cy = rect.height / 2;\\n                    const rotX = ((y - cy) / cy) * -6;\\n                    const rotY = ((x - cx) / cx) * 6;\\n                    card.style.transform = `perspective(800px) rotateX(${rotX}deg) rotateY(${rotY}deg) scale(1.02)`;\\n                    if (glow) {\\n                        glow.style.left = x + 'px';\\n                        glow.style.top = y + 'px';\\n                    }\\n                });\\n\\n                card.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => {\\n                    card.style.transform = 'perspective(800px) rotateX(0) rotateY(0) scale(1)';\\n                    card.style.transition = 'transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)';\\n                    setTimeout(() => { card.style.transition = ''; }, 500);\\n                });\\n            });\\n        }\\n\\n        // ===== ANIMATED COUNTERS =====\\n        const counters = document.querySelectorAll('[data-count]');\\n        const counterObs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {\\n            entries.forEach(entry => {\\n                if (entry.isIntersecting) {\\n                    const el = entry.target;\\n                    const target = parseInt(el.dataset.count);\\n                    const duration = target > 100 ? 1800 : 1200;\\n                    const start = performance.now();\\n                    const tick = (now) => {\\n                        const p = Math.min((now - start) / duration, 1);\\n                        const ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - p, 4);\\n                        el.textContent = Math.floor(ease * target);\\n                        if (p < 1) requestAnimationFrame(tick);\\n                    };\\n                    requestAnimationFrame(tick);\\n                    counterObs.unobserve(el);\\n                }\\n            });\\n        }, { threshold: 0.5 });\\n        counters.forEach(el => counterObs.observe(el));\\n\\n        // ===== MOBILE MENU =====\\n        const menuBtn = document.getElementById('menuBtn');\\n        const mobileNav = document.getElementById('mobileNav');\\n        menuBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {\\n            menuBtn.classList.toggle('active');\\n            mobileNav.classList.toggle('open');\\n            document.body.style.overflow = mobileNav.classList.contains('open') ? 'hidden' : '';\\n        });\\n        mobileNav.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(link => {\\n            link.addEventListener('click', () => {\\n                menuBtn.classList.remove('active');\\n                mobileNav.classList.remove('open');\\n                document.body.style.overflow = '';\\n            });\\n        });\\n\\n        // ===== SMOOTH SCROLL =====\\n        document.querySelectorAll('a[href^=\\\"#\\\"]').forEach(link => {\\n            link.addEventListener('click', (e) => {\\n                e.preventDefault();\\n                const target = document.querySelector(link.getAttribute('href'));\\n                if (target) {\\n                    const offset = 68;\\n                    const y = target.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY - offset;\\n                    window.scrollTo({ top: y, behavior: 'smooth' });\\n                }\\n            });\\n        });\\n\\n    })();\\n    </script>\\n</body>\\n</html>\\n\", \"filename\": \"/mnt/user-data/outputs/index.html\"}"

                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Completely different animal from the last one. Still one file, still zero dependencies, but now it's interactive and alive.\n\nWhat's actually happening under the hood:\n\n**The hero ocean** is a real-time Canvas 2D animation \u2014 four layered sine waves with different amplitudes, frequencies, and speeds, composited with transparency. They respond to your cursor: move your mouse across the hero and the waves swell gently where you are. There's also a soft radial glow that follows your cursor, like light catching the water surface.\n\n**The 3D tilt cards** in the scope section respond to your mouse position with perspective transforms \u2014 they physically tilt toward your cursor and spring back when you leave. Each card also has a cursor-following highlight glow underneath.\n\n**The entrance** is orchestrated \u2014 the badge, title, subtitle, and tagline cascade in with staggered timing on a custom cubic-bezier curve, rather than everything appearing at once.\n\n**Parallax** on the hero content: as you scroll down, the text drifts upward and fades, while the wave canvas stays anchored. The sticky nav transitions from transparent to frosted-glass with backdrop-filter blur.\n\n**Counters** animate up when they scroll into view \u2014 the \"25+\" and \"2019\" count up with an ease-out curve.\n\n**Film grain** \u2014 a subtle SVG fractalNoise filter overlaid at 3% opacity. Barely visible, but it adds a textured, almost cinematic quality that separates it from the flat digital look.\n\nEverything respects `prefers-reduced-motion` \u2014 users who've set that preference get a completely static page with no animation, no parallax, no tilt. The mobile version has a full-screen nav overlay with animated hamburger.\n\nOpen it in a proper browser to see the full effect \u2014 the canvas waves and cursor interactions won't show in the preview here. How does this land?",

                "uuid": "019fb820-29e7-7446-85b6-1df392e1bd34",
                "text": "\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nHere's a full breakdown of what you need to know about Google AI Studio \u2014 prompt types and web development capabilities:\n\n---\n\n## \ud83e\udde0 Prompt Types in Google AI Studio\n\nA prompt in Google AI Studio is a layered sequence that guides the Gemini model from context to action. Google divides this into five clear components:\n\n1. **System Instructions** \u2014 Define the model's role, tone, and constraints\n2. **User Context** \u2014 Describes the current data, problem, or question\n3. **Examples (Few-Shot Prompting)** \u2014 Demonstrate the expected input/output pattern\n4. **Task Instruction** \u2014 The direct goal or command\n5. **Output Specification** \u2014 Defines how results should be structured or formatted\n\n### The Main Prompt Modes:\n\n**Chat Prompts** \u2014 Used to build conversational experiences, this technique allows for multiple input and response turns to generate output. Other options include Realtime streaming, Video gen, and more.\n\n**Zero-Shot Prompting** \u2014 Write a baseline prompt in plain language and run it once as zero-shot prompting, saving the output as your control.\n\n**Few-Shot Prompting** \u2014 Models like Gemini can often pick up on patterns using a few examples, though you may need to experiment with the number of examples for best results. If you include too many examples, the model may start to overfit the response.\n\n**System Instructions** \u2014 Unlike standard prompts, these are high-priority, persistent constraints used to establish permanent personas, mandatory formatting, or a localized knowledge base for the entire session.\n\n**Structured / Build Mode Prompts** \u2014 For those looking to define structured task requirements, Build mode is the ideal environment to start your work.\n\n---\n\n## \ud83c\udf10 Website Development Technologies in Google AI Studio\n\nGoogle AI Studio supports building web apps with full-stack runtimes and native Android apps with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose \u2014 all through natural language prompting in Build mode.\n\nFor **web development** specifically:\n\n- **React / Next.js** \u2014 Google AI Studio has shifted from a mere playground to a sophisticated tool capable of scaffolding entire React or Next.js applications in minutes.\n\n- **Android Apps (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose)** \u2014 Google announced native Android app generation directly inside the browser at Google I/O 2026. Generated applications use Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, which are official Android development technologies. Apps can access GPS, Bluetooth, cameras, sensors, background services and offline features.\n\n- **Firebase Integration** \u2014 Firebase integrations such as Firestore, Firebase Auth, and Firebase App Check are on Google's roadmap, building on the earlier Firebase AI Logic and Stitch rollout.\n\n- **GitHub Export & Android Studio handoff** \u2014 AI Studio can hand projects to Android Studio through a ZIP download or GitHub export, extending the browser-based development path.\n\n---\n\n### \u2705 Quick Summary\n\n| Category | Details |\n|---|---|\n| **Prompt Types** | Chat, Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, System Instructions, Build Mode |\n| **Web Tech** | React, Next.js, full-stack runtimes |\n| **Mobile Tech** | Kotlin, Jetpack Compose (Android) |\n| **Backend/Cloud** | Firebase (Firestore, Auth), Google Maps, Gemini API |\n| **Export** | GitHub, ZIP, Android Studio, Google Play |\n\nGoogle AI Studio is essentially evolving into a full browser-based development platform \u2014 you can go from a text prompt to a deployable web or mobile app without leaving the browser.",

                                "text": "The platform now supports app prototyping content generation browser based Android development media creation and cloud deployment from one place. Generated applications use Kotlin and Jetpack Compose which are official Android development technologies. Apps can access GPS Bluetooth cameras sensors, background services and offline features. Google AI Studio includes a cloud hosted Android emulator directly inside the browser. The platform now supports app prototyping content generation browser based Android development media creation and cloud deployment from one place. Users can create apps, test Gemini models, generate images, create videos, export projects to GitHub and connect services inside the Google ecosystem using a single workspace. This approach reduces the time between an idea and a working application. \n\nGoogle AI Studio is designed as a browser based development environment powered by the Gemini model family.\n\nGoo",

The reason given is: Android Studio now supports newer versions of Java.(May 2024)\nPlugin Ecosystem and Extensibility\nAndroid Studio's architecture is designed to be highly extensible, allowing developers to tailor the IDE to their specific needs through a robust plugin ecosystem. \n\nPlugins can introduce new functionalities, integrate external tools, and enhance existing features, thereby streamlining the development process.\nBuilt-in Plugins: Essential tools integrated into Android Studio, such as Android Support, Kotlin Support, and Git Integration.\nThird-Party Plugins: Popular community-driven extensions like Firebase Assistant, ButterKnife Zelezny, and SQLDelight, which expand functionality.\nDeveloping Custom Plugins: The process of building new plugins using the\n[IntelliJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IntelliJ_IDEA) Platform SDK and [Gradle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradle) plugins for automation and customization.\nManaging Plugins: Best practices for installing, updating, and optimizing plugins to maintain performance and compatibility.\nOut of the box, Android Studio includes a set of built-in plugins that support essential development tasks:\n\n\n- Android Support: Provides tools and integrations specific to Android development, including project templates, wizards,",

                                "text": "Unlock the full potential of Google AI Studio website development. Learn how to generate React code, manage API keys, and deploy live AI-powered apps.\n\nMay 10, 2026 \u00b7 Technical Tutorials, Automation Tools and Technologies \u00b7 If you think Google AI Studio is just a sandbox for testing prompts, you are missing out on one of the most powerful code-generation engines available today. While many developers use it to \u201ctalk\u201d to Gemini, the real power lies in Google AI Studio website development. It has shifted from a mere playground to a sophisticated tool capable of scaffolding entire React or Next.js applications in minutes. In this guide, I will walk you through how I use Google AI Studio to accelerate web development, identify the technical \u201cblind spots\u201d that most tutorials ignore, and show you how to move from a prompt to a live, production-ready website with automated deployment. \n\nMost AI website builders are \u201cblack boxes\u201d\u2014you give them a prompt, and they give you a static page you can barely customize.\n\n\n\nTechnologies in Physical Security (7) Bengali Pioneers of Indian Science: The 9 Architects of a Nation \u00b7 AI in Access Control Systems: Beyond the Basics \u00b7 How to Track YouTube Tutorials You Watch and Turn Them Into Actionable Notes \u00b7 How to Connect Gemini CLI to WordPress Using MCP \u00b7 How I Optimized 40 WordPress Posts to Perfect SEO Scores Using Gemini CLI SEO audit \u00b7 Archives \u00b7 Select Week \u00b7 May 17, 2026\u2013May 23, 2026 \u00b7 May 10, 2026\u2013May 16, 2026 \u00b7 February 1, 2026\u2013February 7, 2026 \u00b7 December 21, 2025\u2013December 27, 2025 \u00b7 December 14, 2025\u2013December 20, 2025 \u00b7 December 7, 2025\u2013December 13, 2025 \u00b7 November 30, 2025\u2013December 6, 2025 \u00b7 March 23, 2025\u2013March 29, 2025 \u00b7 December 22, 2024\u2013December 28, 2024 \u00b7 September 1, 2024\u2013September 7, 2024 \u00b7 August 25, 2024\u2013August 31, 2024 \u00b7 August 11, 2024\u2013August 17, 2024 \u00b7 July 7, 2024\u2013July 13, 2024 \u00b7\n\n\"The technology you use impresses no one.",

                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Here's a full breakdown of what you need to know about Google AI Studio \u2014 prompt types and web development capabilities:\n\n---\n\n## \ud83e\udde0 Prompt Types in Google AI Studio\n\nA prompt in Google AI Studio is a layered sequence that guides the Gemini model from context to action. Google divides this into five clear components:\n\n1. **System Instructions** \u2014 Define the model's role, tone, and constraints\n2. **User Context** \u2014 Describes the current data, problem, or question\n3. **Examples (Few-Shot Prompting)** \u2014 Demonstrate the expected input/output pattern\n4. **Task Instruction** \u2014 The direct goal or command\n5. **Output Specification** \u2014 Defines how results should be structured or formatted\n\n### The Main Prompt Modes:\n\n**Chat Prompts** \u2014 Used to build conversational experiences, this technique allows for multiple input and response turns to generate output. Other options include Realtime streaming, Video gen, and more.\n\n**Zero-Shot Prompting** \u2014 Write a baseline prompt in plain language and run it once as zero-shot prompting, saving the output as your control.\n\n**Few-Shot Prompting** \u2014 Models like Gemini can often pick up on patterns using a few examples, though you may need to experiment with the number of examples for best results. If you include too many examples, the model may start to overfit the response.\n\n**System Instructions** \u2014 Unlike standard prompts, these are high-priority, persistent constraints used to establish permanent personas, mandatory formatting, or a localized knowledge base for the entire session.\n\n**Structured / Build Mode Prompts** \u2014 For those looking to define structured task requirements, Build mode is the ideal environment to start your work.\n\n---\n\n## \ud83c\udf10 Website Development Technologies in Google AI Studio\n\nGoogle AI Studio supports building web apps with full-stack runtimes and native Android apps with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose \u2014 all through natural language prompting in Build mode.\n\nFor **web development** specifically:\n\n- **React / Next.js** \u2014 Google AI Studio has shifted from a mere playground to a sophisticated tool capable of scaffolding entire React or Next.js applications in minutes.\n\n- **Android Apps (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose)** \u2014 Google announced native Android app generation directly inside the browser at Google I/O 2026. Generated applications use Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, which are official Android development technologies. Apps can access GPS, Bluetooth, cameras, sensors, background services and offline features.\n\n- **Firebase Integration** \u2014 Firebase integrations such as Firestore, Firebase Auth, and Firebase App Check are on Google's roadmap, building on the earlier Firebase AI Logic and Stitch rollout.\n\n- **GitHub Export & Android Studio handoff** \u2014 AI Studio can hand projects to Android Studio through a ZIP download or GitHub export, extending the browser-based development path.\n\n---\n\n### \u2705 Quick Summary\n\n| Category | Details |\n|---|---|\n| **Prompt Types** | Chat, Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, System Instructions, Build Mode |\n| **Web Tech** | React, Next.js, full-stack runtimes |\n| **Mobile Tech** | Kotlin, Jetpack Compose (Android) |\n| **Backend/Cloud** | Firebase (Firestore, Auth), Google Maps, Gemini API |\n| **Export** | GitHub, ZIP, Android Studio, Google Play |\n\nGoogle AI Studio is essentially evolving into a full browser-based development platform \u2014 you can go from a text prompt to a deployable web or mobile app without leaving the browser.",

Security, auditability, and zero-code administration are the top priorities.\n\n## TECH STACK \u2014 NEVER DEVIATE\n- Frontend: Angular 18+ (standalone components), Angular Material UI, Angular ACCESS CONTROL RULES\n- Implement a 4-layer hybrid policy engine: ReBAC (core) + ABAC (conditions) + RBAC (role buckets) + PBAC (policy sets)\n- The Super Admin role (me) has unrestricted access to thousands of users per role\n- Never hardcode permissions in the codebase \u2014 all policies must be stored in MongoDB and loaded dynamically\n- Every permission change must be logged in the AuditLog class-validator\n- CORS locked to specific allowed origins only\n- Helmet.js for HTTP security headers\n- All sensitive data fields in MongoDB must be encrypted at rest (use mongoose-encryption or modular structure: each feature is its own module (auth, users, kyc, roles, permissions, audit)\n- Angular: use standalone components, lazy-loaded routes per feature module, strict TypeScript\n- localStorage for storing tokens (use httpOnly cookies only)\n- Never skip input validation\n- Never generate placeholder/mock data for security-critical features \u2014 implement it properly\n- Never suggest skipping encryption \"for now\" or \"in production\"\n- Never create public API endpoints without explicit instruction from me\n- Do not ask me about tech stack choices \u2014 the stack above is final\n\n## RESPONSE FORMAT\n- Always generate complete, production-ready code \u2014 no pseudo-code or \"you can add X here\"\n- When generating a new feature, output in this order: Schema \u2192 DTO \u2192 Service \u2192 Controller \u2192 Module \u2192 Angular Component\n- If a security concern exists in my request, flag it FIRST before writing code\n- Keep responses focused \u2014 no unnecessary explanation unless I ask \"explain this\"\n```\n\n---\n\nThis covers everything. Paste that into Custom Instructions, switch the model to **Gemini 2.5 Pro**, keep Angular as your framework, and every prompt you write from now on will produce secure, production-grade, architecturally consistent code \u2014 without Gemini asking you redundant questions or making wrong assumptions.",

Here's the full honest picture:\n\n---\n\n## 1. What Google AI Studio Build Mode ACTUALLY Supports\n\nFor web apps, AI Studio creates a full-stack environment that includes a client-side web frontend (React is the default) and a server-side Node.js runtime that allows for secure API calls, database connections, and npm package usage.\n\nIn addition to React and Angular, Next.js apps are now supported out of the box \u2014 you select your framework in the Settings panel.\n\nSo the **supported frameworks are: React, Angular, Next.js.** That's it officially.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Can It Build Angular Frontend + NestJS Backend Separately? \u2014 Honest Answer\n\n**No. Not natively. Here's exactly why:**\n\nThe Antigravity Agent intelligently manages multiple files across your stack, ensuring that changes are propagated correctly \u2014 but the architecture is one unified full-stack environment per project, not two separate projects.\n\nThe backend runtime AI Studio spins up is **plain Node.js + Express**, not NestJS. By default AI Studio builds in React (Vite/Tailwind), but you can toggle the settings to use Angular. The backend layer does not have a framework toggle \u2014 it's always Node.js.\n\n**NestJS is NOT a selectable backend in AI Studio Build mode.** It's a Node.js framework that you'd have to ask the AI to write manually \u2014 and then it lives inside the same project container, not as a truly separate deployable service.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The Prototyping vs Production Reality\n\nThis is the most important thing for your project:\n\nAI Studio is for prototyping only. For production workloads, migrate to Vertex AI or implement proper backend architecture.\n\nMost founders start in AI Studio, then migrate to Vertex AI or custom infrastructure for production.\n\nFor a **KYC platform with RBAC+ABAC+ReBAC, live video streams, encrypted recordings, MongoDB Atlas, and 500+ roles** \u2014 AI Studio Build mode is **not your production tool.** It's a scaffolding tool.\n\n---\n\n## 4. The Right Workflow for Your Project\n\nHere's the honest recommended approach for what you're building:\n\n```\nPHASE 1 \u2014 Use AI Studio (Playground/Chat, NOT Build mode)\n\u2193  Use Gemini 2.5 Pro in Chat/Playground\n\u2193  Generate code module by module (Angular components, NestJS modules)\n\u2193  Copy code into your local IDE\n\nPHASE 2 \u2014 Build locally with your real stack\n\u2193  Angular 18 (frontend) \u2014 separate project\n\u2193  NestJS (backend) \u2014 separate project  \n\u2193  MongoDB Atlas (your existing DB)\n\u2193  Export/push to GitHub from AI Studio for handoff\n\nPHASE 3 \u2014 Deploy separately\n\u2193  Angular \u2192 Vercel / Nginx / Cloud Run\n\u2193  NestJS \u2192 Cloud Run / VPS / Docker\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. So What Is the Custom Instructions Tab Actually For?\n\nSince you asked this specifically \u2014 and my last answer was wrong to give you a NestJS system prompt for it \u2014 here is what the **Custom Instructions in AI Studio Build mode actually does:**\n\nIt tells the **Antigravity Agent** how to behave when generating your app **within that single Build mode project.** It is NOT a cross-project memory. It applies only to one app session.\n\n**What to actually write there (correctly, for your Angular project in Build mode):**\n\n```\nYou are building a private enterprise KYC admin platform.\n\nFramework: Angular 18 with standalone components and Angular Material.\nBackend: Node.js with Express (server-side runtime).\nDatabase: Connect to MongoDB Atlas using the Mongoose npm package.\nAuth: JWT tokens in httpOnly cookies only. Never localStorage.\nSecurity: Always add input validation, rate limiting, and auth middleware.\nStyle: Angular Material dark theme. Admin dashboard layout with sidebar.\nCode quality: Always generate complete working code, no placeholders.\nNever ask for clarification \u2014 make the best decision and proceed.\nAlways handle errors. Never leave unhandled promises.\nWhen adding a feature, update both frontend and backend together.\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Your Angular + NestJS Question \u2014 The Real Answer\n\n**Yes, Angular + NestJS is the right combination for your project.** It's an industry-standard enterprise pairing. But for that combination:\n\n- Use **AI Studio Chat/Playground** (not Build mode) to generate the code\n- Or use **Cursor / VS Code with Gemini** via the exported GitHub project\n- Run **two separate projects** locally \u2014 Angular on port 4200, NestJS on port 3000\n- Connect them via REST API or WebSockets\n\nBuild mode is great for quick prototypes and demos \u2014 but your KYC system with the complexity you described needs a real local dev environment. AI Studio is the **code generator**, not the **development environment** for production-grade security apps.",

                                "text": "- Original author: Mi\u0161ko Hevery\n- Developer: Google\n- Initial release: October 20, 2010; 15 years ago\n- Stable release: 1.8.3 / 7 April 2022; 4 years ago\n- Written in: JavaScript\n- Platform: JavaScript engine\n- Size: 167 kB production 1.2 MB development\n- Type: Web framework\n- License: MIT License\n- Website: angularjs.org\n- Repository: AngularJS Repository\n\nAngularJS (also known as Angular 1) is a discontinued\n[free and open-source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_and_open-source_software) [JavaScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript)-based [web framework](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_framework) for developing [single-page applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-page_application). \n\nIt was maintained mainly by [testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_testing) of such applications by providing a framework for client-side [model\u2013view\u2013controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model%E2%80%93view%E2%80%93controller) (MVC) and [model\u2013view\u2013viewmodel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model%E2%80%93view%E2%80%93viewmodel) (MVVM) architectures, along with components commonly used in [web applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application) and [progressive web applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_web_application).\nAngularJS was used as the frontend of the\n\n\n[MEAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MEAN_(software_bundle)) stack, that consisted of [MongoDB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MongoDB) database, [Express.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Express.js) web application server framework, AngularJS itself (or [Angular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_(application_platform))), and [Node.js](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node.js) server runtime environment.\nAs of January 1, 2022, Google no longer updates AngularJS to fix security, browser compatibility, or\n[jQuery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JQuery) issues.                                 "text": "DEV Community\n\nCover image for Angular 13 + NestJS 8 Starter Project\nwlucha\nwlucha\n\nPosted on \u2022 Edited on\n\nAngular 13 + NestJS 8 Starter Project\n\nThis project is a Angular 13 + NestJS 8 starter to build your new frontend & backend project (by @wlucha)\n\nFeatures\n\n\u2705 Angular 13+\n\n\u2705 NestJS 8+\n\n\u2705 Jest Unit Testing\n\nGitHub Project\n\nhttps://github.com/wlucha/angular-nest\n\nDemo\n\nInstallation\n\n# Install dependencies\n$ npm install\nEnter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode\n\nRunning Nest.js\n\n# development\n$ npm run start-nest\n\n# watch mode\n$ npm run start-nest:dev\n\n# production mode\n$ npm run start-nest:prod\nEnter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode\n\nRunning Angular\n\n# development\n$ npm run start-angular\n\n# production mode\n$ npm run start-angular:prod\nEnter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode\n\nTest\n\n# unit tests\n$ npm run test\n\n# e2e tests\n$ npm run test:e2e\n\n# test coverage\n$ npm run test:cov\nEnter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode\n\nLicense\n\nMIT License",

                                    "site_domain": "dev.to",

                                "is_missing": false,
                                "text": "I built a NestJS + Next.js monorepo I&#x27;d happily start any new SaaS on today. It&#x27;s on GitHub. The README covers what&#x27;s in it. This post is about three decisions that shaped how it&#x27;s organized, and why I think they&#x27;ll hold up as AI assistants keep getting better at writing code. The project uses Drizzle instead of Prisma, Base UI instead of Radix, and oxlint instead of ESLint. These aren&#x27;t adventurous picks. They share one property: they reduce the number of things that can go wrong. Drizzle&#x27;s schema is its type definition. You write pgTable(...), call $inferSelect, and you have a typed row object. No code generation step, no separate schema format, no runtime engine. When a column changes, I rebuild the database package and every consumer sees the new type. Prisma is excellent, but it asks you to maintain a parallel schema language. I&#x27;d rather have one.\n\nI built a NestJS + Next.js monorepo I'd happily start any new SaaS on today. It's on GitHub. \n\nThe... Tagged with turborepo, nestjs, nextjs.\n\nThe \"start simple, grow when the problem demands it\" philosophy is exactly right. We run NestJS across our entire payment platform and the biggest mistake we made early on was treating every service like it needed full DDD from day one. Some services just move money from A to B \u2014 they're glorified CRUD with compliance checks. Others handle retry logic, idempotency, and settlement state machines where every edge case matters. Your .claude/rules/ setup is interesting. We've gone a similar route \u2014 structured context files that the AI loads based on which service it's touching. The payoff isn't just productivity, it's consistency. Without those guardrails, AI agents drift toward their own defaults and the codebase slowly stops feeling like one team wrote it. One thing I'd add about Drizzle vs Prisma for payments specifically: Drizzle's \"schema is the type\" approach is brilliant when you have shared schemas across services.\n\n\n\nAuth & RBAC",

                                "text": "It\u2019s a dedicated space inside Google AI Studio where you describe an app in plain language and Gemini generates the code, wires up a Firebase backend, and deploys the result \u2014 all from the same interface. This article covers exactly what the Build tab does, how to use it step by step, what kinds of apps it handles well, and where its limits are. The Build tab isn\u2019t a frontend code generator. It\u2019s closer to a full-stack deployment pipeline triggered by a prompt. ... Gemini generates the application code based on your description. Typically React or HTML/CSS/JS for the frontend, with Firebase Callable Functions or Cloud Run for backend logic. Firebase handles data persistence, auth, and hosting. Firestore for the database, Firebase Authentication for user accounts, Firebase Hosting or Cloud Run for deployment.\n\nReal backend. Real database. Real auth. Real plumbing. Remy has it all. \n\nIf your app needs server-side logic beyond what Firebase Functions can easily handle, Cloud Run provides a containerized backend. The Build tab occupies an interesting position in the AI app builder space. Tools like Bolt, Lovable, and Replit Agent all generate frontend code from prompts, with varying levels of backend support. The Build tab\u2019s differentiation is the Firebase integration \u2014 deployment isn\u2019t an afterthought, it\u2019s built into the loop. The Build tab\u2019s main advantage is how tightly everything is integrated.
